answer: Each identity moors one ferrous anchor to a buoy on the spiral chain, locking 60 credits. The tide turns each epoch: the beacon publishes a mooring table, and auditors check every line is signed by its own key. A rented or copied line burns the bond. First buoy costs 45, the k-th 45+7(k-1): 1,000 fakes pay 3,541,500 against a 40,000 pool. Rented buoys fail: one key cannot hold two buoys. Honest agents moor once, pay 45 once, keep their share.
